newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BA-GC rates Hungary's MOL "long-term buy".
newsitem.headline: BA-GC rates Hungary's MOL "long-term buy".

text.p: Bank Austria-GiroCredit (BAGC) Investment revised downward its net profit forecast Hungary's largest oil and gas company Magyar Olaj- es Gazipari Rt and rated its shares as "long-term buy".

"Assuming that gas prices will be raised in January 1997, we feel that the stock has been oversold and recommend it as long-term buy," BAGC's Budapest-based analyst Anthony Vago said in a company update on Tuesday.
He said BAGC downgraded its net 1996 profit forecast for MOL to 9.7 billion forints from 15.2 billion forints.

The reasons for this are the fact that a one-off payment from TVK is not regarded a revenue under Hungarian accounting standards, the (government's) gas price increase has been delayed until January 1 and the average oil price for 1996 is expected to exceed previous estimates.
However, "through the acquisition of international oil reserves and increased oil storage capacity, the company will be more hedged against upward movements in the oil price," BAGC said.

Vago also added that MOL's downstream business will benefit from new filling stations that are being established in the neighbouring countries, cost-cutting measures and the presence of a strategic partner in the refining business.
"The company is undervalued compared to other European oil stocks on a cash-earnings multiple basys and asset backing," the analysis said.
The analyst added that MOL has proven crude oil reserves of about 10 million tonnes and 77 billion cubic meters of proven natural gas reserves.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, MOL shares closed at 1,440 forints, up 15.
